drug_class: Combination antiretroviral (HIV medicine) — includes two NRTIs and one NNRTI
purpose: This medicine is used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults and certain adolescents. It helps keep the amount of HIV virus in your body very low so your immune system can stay strong. It does not cure HIV, but it helps you stay healthier and reduces the risk of passing HIV to others.
how_it_works: This pill combines three medicines that each attack HIV in slightly different ways. Two of them (emtricitabine and tenofovir alafenamide) block a tool the virus needs to copy itself, and the third one (rilpivirine) blocks a different step in that same copying process. Together, they work as a team to keep the virus from multiplying in your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, trouble sleeping or unusual dreams, nausea, dizziness, depressed mood, and rash. These often get better after the first few weeks as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Do not take this medicine with antacids, certain heartburn medicines, or supplements containing calcium, iron, or magnesium within a certain timeframe, as they can make the medicine stop working properly. Tell your doctor if you feel very sad, hopeless, or have thoughts of hurting yourself, as mood changes can occur. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first — stopping suddenly can make HIV harder to treat. Also, let your doctor know if you have any liver or kidney problems before starting.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once a day WITH a meal. Taking it with food is very important — it helps your body absorb the medicine properly. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep it working its best.
